records.title: Annual quarantine of sport-harvested mussels
records.summary: Sport-harvested mussels from the entire California coast, including bays and estuaries, may not be harvested for human consumption (bait only).
records.official_text: The quarantine begins May 1 and applies to all species of mussels that are recreationally harvested for human consumption along the California coast, including all bays and estuaries. During the quarantine, mussels may only be harvested for use as bait.

area.description: Along the California coast, including all bays and estuaries
area.geometry_note: Statewide; not drawn on the map.

records.expected_end_note: CDPH (Sept 14, 2026): the quarantine "will continue through at least October 31." It can be extended; an end date is not confirmed until CDPH announces it.

sources.label: CDPH SN26-008: Annual quarantine of sport-harvested mussels begins May 1
CDPH SN26-018 (states the quarantine continues through at least October 31)

uncertainties: Applies to sport-harvested mussels; commercially harvested mussels from certified dealers are regulated separately by CDPH.

records.title: Do not eat sport-harvested bivalve shellfish from Monterey County
records.summary: CDPH advises not eating sport-harvested mussels, clams, scallops or oysters from Monterey County because of dangerous levels of domoic acid detected in mussels.
records.official_text: CDPH is advising the public not to eat sport-harvested mussels, clams, scallops, or oysters, gathered from Monterey County due to dangerous levels of domoic acid toxin detected in mussels from Monterey County.

area.geometry_note: CDPH county polygon from the CDPH shellfish advisory map; the advisory applies to shellfish gathered from the county, not to a line at sea.

sources.label: CDPH recreational bivalve shellfish advisory map

records.title: Do not eat northern anchovies from Pigeon Point to Point Lobos
records.summary: CDPH advises not eating northern anchovies harvested between Pigeon Point (San Mateo County) and Point Lobos (Monterey County) because of dangerous levels of domoic acid. Does not apply to anchovies taken for bait.
records.official_text: The California Department of Public Health (CDPH) advises the public not to consume northern anchovies harvested from waters between: Pigeon Point, San Mateo County (37° 11.00’ N. lat.) and Point Lobos, Monterey County (36° 31.46’ N. Lat.)

area.description: Waters between Pigeon Point, San Mateo County (37° 11.00’ N) and Point Lobos, Monterey County (36° 31.46’ N)
area.geometry_note: The map shows the notice's official north and south latitude limits as lines drawn 30 km out from the coast (coastline from the C-HARM land/sea mask). The notice states no offshore limit; its wording controls.

uncertainties: The notice states latitudes only; how far offshore it applies is not specified.

records.title: Northern anchovy: no take for human consumption, Pigeon Point to Point Lobos
records.summary: Northern anchovies may not be harvested recreationally or commercially for human consumption in Monterey Bay (Pigeon Point to Point Lobos). Commercially taken anchovies may only be sold as dead bait; recreationally taken anchovies may only be used as bait.
records.official_text: Northern anchovies may not be harvested recreationally or commercially for human consumption in Monterey Bay (Pigeon Point, San Mateo County to Point Lobos, Monterey County) due to elevated levels of domoic acid toxin in the fish. The Monterey Bay closure went into effect on September 11, 2026.

area.description: Monterey Bay: Pigeon Point, San Mateo County (37° 11.000’ N) to Point Lobos, Monterey County (36° 31.461’ N)
area.geometry_note: The map shows the notice's official north and south latitude limits as lines drawn 30 km out from the coast (coastline from the C-HARM land/sea mask). The notice states no offshore limit; its wording controls. Latitudes as recorded from CDFW's Sept 11, 2026 restriction (docs/coastwatch/evidence/sources-regulatory.md).

uncertainties: Offshore extent is not stated on the CDFW status page.

records.title: Recreational razor clam fishery closed in Humboldt County
records.summary: The recreational razor clam fishery remains closed in Humboldt County because of elevated domoic acid in razor clams.
records.official_text: The recreational razor clam fishery remains closed in Humboldt County due to elevated levels of domoic acid in razor clams. The Humboldt County closure has been in effect since May 2, 2024.

area.geometry_note: CDPH county polygon; the closure applies to the county's razor clam beaches.

sources.label: CDFW: Health advisories and closures (razor clam)

records.title: Commercial rock crab: domoic acid closure, 40°00′ N to 40°30′ N
records.summary: A domoic acid fishery closure is in effect for the commercial rock crab fishery from the Mendocino/Humboldt county line to Cape Mendocino.
records.official_text: A Domoic Acid Fishery Closure is in effect for the commercial rock crab fishery from the Mendocino/Humboldt county line (40° 00.00’ N. lat.) to Cape Mendocino, Humboldt County (40° 30.00’ N. lat.).

area.description: Mendocino/Humboldt county line (40° 00.00’ N) to Cape Mendocino, Humboldt County (40° 30.00’ N)
area.geometry_note: The map shows the notice's official north and south latitude limits as lines drawn 30 km out from the coast (coastline from the C-HARM land/sea mask). The notice states no offshore limit; its wording controls.

records.effective_date_note: The CDFW status page does not state when this closure took effect.

sources.label: CDFW: Health advisories and closures (rock crab, commercial)
CDFW Domoic Acid Fishery Closure Information Line (831) 649-2883

records.title: Do not eat rock crab internal organs: CA/OR border to Mendocino/Sonoma line, and Northern Channel Islands
records.summary: CDPH recommends not eating the internal organs (viscera) of rock crab caught from the California/Oregon border to the Mendocino/Sonoma county line, and from waters off Santa Rosa Island and the Northern Channel Islands.
records.official_text: CDPH currently recommends not eating the interal organs of rock crab caught from the California/Oregon border to the Mendocino/Sonoma county line, and from the waters off Santa Rosa Island and the Northern Channel Islands.

area.description: California/Oregon border to the Mendocino/Sonoma county line; and waters off Santa Rosa Island and the Northern Channel Islands
area.geometry_note: The map shows the notice's official north and south latitude limits as lines drawn 30 km out from the coast (coastline from the C-HARM land/sea mask). The notice states no offshore limit; its wording controls. The Mendocino/Sonoma county line latitude (38° 46.125’ N) is taken from CDFW's RAMP zone definitions because the advisory names the line without a coordinate. The Northern Channel Islands portion is not drawn.

records.effective_date_note: Quoted from the CDFW status page (verbatim, including the agency's spelling). The originating CDPH release was not re-read for this record.

sources.label: CDFW: Health advisories and closures (rock crab note)

uncertainties: Effective date not confirmed from the CDPH release.
Northern Channel Islands part of the area is not mapped in CoastWatch.
